successCriteria.description: knexfile.ts exists at project root, declares client 'pg', configures TypeScript migrations (extension 'ts') pointing at a './migrations' directory, and reads its connection string from process.env.DATABASE_URL — the same env var consumed by src/shared/db/connection.ts.

Migration 001 creates the leave_policies table with a UUID primary key defaulted via knex.fn.uuid(), a NOT NULL check-constrained leave_type varchar limited to the six values annual/sick/emergency/unpaid/maternity/paternity, NOT NULL entitlement_days integer, nullable accrual_rate/max_accumulation/minimum_notice_days, NOT NULL booleans requires_manager_approval and is_active both defaulting to true, and NOT NULL timestamptz created_at/updated_at. The migration exports both up and down functions, with down calling dropTableIfExists('leave_policies').

Migration 002 creates the leave_requests table with a UUID PK (knex.fn.uuid()), NOT NULL employee_id and leave_type_id uuid columns where leave_type_id has a foreign key referencing leave_policies.id, NOT NULL start_date/end_date date columns, nullable reason text, a NOT NULL status varchar defaulting to 'DRAFT' with a CHECK constraint over DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED, nullable approver/rejector/canceller uuid and timestamptz columns plus nullable rejection_reason text, and NOT NULL timestamptz created_at/updated_at. Both up and down functions are exported; down drops the table.

Migration 003 creates the leave_balances table with a UUID PK (knex.fn.uuid()), NOT NULL employee_id and leave_type_id uuid columns where leave_type_id has a foreign key referencing leave_policies.id, NOT NULL entitlement_days decimal, NOT NULL used_days and accrued_days decimals both defaulting to 0, NOT NULL year integer, NOT NULL timestamptz created_at/updated_at, and a unique constraint on (employee_id, leave_type_id, year). Both up and down functions are exported; down drops the table.

All three migrations are reversible: running each down function removes the table it created (dropTableIfExists) without affecting tables created by other migrations, and the migrations are orderable so that leave_policies is created before the tables that reference it.

The knexfile and migrations are excluded from the tsc --noEmit build target (they live outside src/, which is the tsconfig rootDir/include scope) and remain valid TypeScript loadable by ts-node at migration runtime, so the build command passes without compile errors from these files.

constraints: knexfile.ts must read its connection string from process.env.DATABASE_URL directly (with dotenv.config()) and must not import src/shared/db/connection.ts, which exports a pg.Pool instance rather than a connection string.

All UUID primary keys must use knex.fn.uuid() as the column default, and all temporal columns (created_at, updated_at, and the nullable action timestamps) must be timestamptz (timestamp with time zone).

leave_type is an inline check-constrained varchar on leave_policies covering exactly 'annual','sick','emergency','unpaid','maternity','paternity' — there is no separate leave_types table, and the foreign keys on leave_requests.leave_type_id and leave_balances.leave_type_id reference leave_policies.id.

Migrations must use knex.schema.createTable for table creation and knex.schema.dropTableIfExists for rollback; each migration file must export both an up and a down async function accepting a Knex instance.
No hardcoded secrets or connection strings — the only database configuration source is the DATABASE_URL environment variable (HARNESS.json constraint no-hardcoded-secrets, severity critical).
No audit table is created in this migration set — GP-002 (audit records) applies to a later phase; this phase covers only leave_policies, leave_requests, and leave_balances.
outOfScope: Seed data / default policy inserts (e.g., annual 20 days, sick 10 days) — deferred to Phase 9 (migrations/004_seed_default_policies.ts).
Audit log / audit_records table creation — deferred to a later phase per GP-002.
Employee or users table migrations — employee identity is assumed to exist from another domain; this phase creates no employee table.
Leave domain model TypeScript types, repository, service, controller, and routes — these are Phases 2–8 and are not part of the migration phase.
Adding a knex migrate script to package.json or CI pipeline wiring — this phase produces the migration files only; operational runner integration is not specified.

entityInvariants.invariant: A leave policy's leave_type must always be one of the six enumerated values enforced by the database CHECK constraint; the policy's active/inactive state is governed by the is_active flag (true by default), and every policy row carries non-null created_at and updated_at timestamps.

A leave request is always linked to a real leave_policies row via the leave_type_id foreign key, begins in the DRAFT status (the column default), and its status may only hold one of the five lifecycle values enforced by the CHECK constraint; the approver, rejector, and canceller identity/timestamp columns are nullable and populated only when the corresponding lifecycle event occurs.

A leave balance row is unique per (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) combination enforced by the unique constraint, is always linked to a real leave_policies row via the leave_type_id foreign key, and starts with used_days and accrued_days at zero (column defaults) regardless of entitlement.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Knex migration up — each of migrations 001, 002, 003 must export an async up(knex) function that, when executed against a PostgreSQL database, creates its target table with all specified columns, constraints, foreign keys, and check constraints.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: A failed up must leave the database in a state where re-running the migration can succeed; partial table creation should be rolled back by Knex's transactional migration wrapper.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Knex migration down — each of migrations 001, 002, 003 must export an async down(knex) function that drops its target table via dropTableIfExists, fully reversing the up operation.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: down must not throw if the table does not already exist (dropTableIfExists semantics); it must be safe to run repeatedly.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Knex config export — knexfile.ts must export a default Knex.Config object that the knex CLI can load to locate and run the TypeScript migrations in the ./migrations directory against the DATABASE_URL-configured PostgreSQL instance.
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No application auth applies; database access is governed by the credentials embedded in DATABASE_URL.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: knexfile.ts must derive its database connection from the same DATABASE_URL environment variable that src/shared/db/connection.ts uses for its pg.Pool, so that migrations and the application runtime target the same PostgreSQL instance.

The table names, column names, check-constrained enum values (leave_type six values; status five values), foreign-key targets (leave_type_id → leave_policies.id), and the unique constraint on (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) must match the "Database Schema (as built — migrations 001–003)" section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, which is the authoritative schema description.

The migrations directory and knexfile.ts must remain outside the tsc compilation scope defined by tsconfig.json (rootDir ./src, include ['src']) so that the build command (tsc --noEmit) does not attempt to compile them; they are executed via ts-node at migration runtime instead.

The knexfile must be loadable with the knex version declared in package.json (knex ^3.1.0) and the pg client (^8.7.1); the migration files must use only the Knex schema-builder API available in that version (createTable, dropTableIfExists, knex.fn.uuid, knex.raw for CHECK constraints).

integrationPoints.why: The knexfile and migrations execute against the same PostgreSQL instance the application connects to through src/shared/db/connection.ts; migrations create the schema that later-phase repositories will query.

The migration-created tables (leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances) are the schema that the repository layer (Phase 3+) will access through the shared pg.Pool; the knexfile reuses the same DATABASE_URL env var to guarantee schema and runtime target the same database.

The knexfile's default export and the migration files' up/down exports are the contract consumed by the Knex CLI (loaded via ts-node) to apply and roll back schema changes; no npm script is added in this phase but the files must conform to the Knex migration loader's expected shape.

The leave_policies table created by migration 001 is the target into which the later-phase seed migration will insert default policies; the column shape and check constraint established here govern what seed data is valid.
